answer: Here is one mechanism that works: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because lagoon only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, copper is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any pulse approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
